content:
Here is the context and data for the week of 2026-08-17:

        ASX 200 closed last week at 8,847 points.

        Key themes:
        - RBA meeting on Tuesday 18 August — market pricing 68% chance of a 25bps cut to 3.60%
        - US CPI for July printed at 2.7% YoY, slightly above the 2.6% consensus
        - S&P 500 closed at 5,712 — up 0.8% on the week
        - Iron ore at USD 98.50 per tonne — holding below the USD 100 level
        - Gold at USD 3,285 per oz — near record highs
        - Big banks reporting: CBA full-year results due Wednesday 19 August
        - Oil at USD 74.20 per barrel — steady
        - AUD/USD at 0.6415

        

Post 1

RBA cuts 68% priced in — but US CPI at 2.7% YoY just complicated the global rate story. ASX at 8,847 closed the week firm. View is cautiously bullish: the cut happens, but the follow-through depends on CBA's read Wednesday. #ASX #RBA #ausbiz

Post 2

🏦 Banks hinge on CBA Wednesday — full-year numbers set the tone for the sector. ⛏️ Mining stays hostage to iron ore at USD 98.50/t, stuck below USD 100 — the line that separates sentiment from conviction. #ASX #banking #ironore #mining

Post 3

🪙 Gold names deserve attention this week. With spot at USD 3,285/oz near record highs and global rate uncertainty rising post US CPI, producers leveraged to price hold the strongest near-term case. #ASX #gold #ausbiz

Post 4

S&P 500 at 5,712, up 0.8% last week, offers a constructive backdrop — but US CPI at 2.7% YoY above the 2.6% consensus muddies Fed cut timing. AUD/USD at 0.6415 keeps import cost pressure alive. #ASX #ausbiz #inflation #Fed

Post 5

RBA Tuesday 18 Aug: 68% priced for a 25bps cut to 3.60%. Cut delivered = rate-sensitive sectors rally. Surprise hold = AUD spikes, banks and property sold off hard. Which way are you positioned? #ASX #RBA #interestrates #ausbiz

Post 1

📉 Earnings season hit the ASX hard. The index fell 42pts to 9,073.20 (-0.46%), down 1.73% over five days. Consumer names got crushed — results disappointed and the market showed zero mercy. #ASX #ausbiz

Post 2

🔻 Consumer Discretionary worst sector at -3.00%, Financials close behind at -1.76%. Materials the clear bright spot, up +1.76%, with Energy adding +0.93%. Two-speed market: commodities vs everything else. #ASX #mining #ausbiz

Post 3

JBH dropped AUD 10.06 to $71.65 (-12.31%) — the session's sharpest single-stock sell-off. Results underwhelmed, and with consumer confidence fragile, the market priced in a harder road ahead. #ASX #retail #ausbiz

Post 4

🪙 Gold at AUD 6,196.57/oz with AUD/USD at 0.7116. Materials sector strength today tracks directly here — local gold prices near record levels keep miners well-supported even as broader equities slide. #ASX #gold #mining

Post 5

ASX sits 2.40% below its 52-week high. Watch whether Materials can hold that +1.76% buffer as Wall St digests its own earnings week. Bull or bear from here — what's your read? #ASX #ausbiz #investing
